Baseline rate constants

Source: R/rates.R
default_rates.Rd

Returns the model's baseline parameter set as a named list, ready to be passed to simulate_spatial(), simulate_mean_field() or simulate_mean_field_stochastic() via do.call(), or used as a starting point whose individual entries can be overridden. These are the values every simulate function uses by default. Time is in years.

Usage

default_rates()

Value

A named list with the vegetation turnover rates (L_01, L_02, L_12, L_21), the vegetation death rates (L_10, L_20, both 0), the fire burnout rate (L_30, i.e. \(\lambda^{F\emptyset}\)), the two species' spontaneous ignition rates (Lig_13, Lig_23), and the dimensionless xi_nat, xi_inv, eta_nat, eta_inv (see xi2lambda()).

Details

Under this parametrization the native species replaces the invader twice as fast as the reverse, so without fire the invader cannot spread; its advantages are spontaneous ignition, a higher fire-spread probability and post-fire regrowth. See ForestFireR-model for the mechanism and xi2lambda() for the dimensionless probabilities.

See also

xi2lambda(), ForestFireR-model

Examples

str(default_rates())
#> List of 13
#>  $ L_01   : num 0.03
#>  $ L_02   : num 0.03
#>  $ L_10   : num 0
#>  $ L_20   : num 0
#>  $ L_12   : num 0.005
#>  $ L_21   : num 0.01
#>  $ L_30   : num 1e+06
#>  $ Lig_13 : num 0
#>  $ Lig_23 : num 1e-04
#>  $ xi_nat : num 0.5
#>  $ xi_inv : num 0.6
#>  $ eta_nat: num 0
#>  $ eta_inv: num 0.6

# Run with the baseline set, raising only the invader's regrowth advantage
pars <- default_rates()
pars$eta_inv <- 0.8
pars[c("L_10", "L_20")] <- NULL          # not arguments of the simulate functions
mf <- do.call(simulate_mean_field, c(list(T = 200), pars))
tail(mf, 1)
#>       time        n0         n1        n2           n3           n4        n5
#> 201 200.01 0.3267421 0.02260069 0.6506568 4.601405e-08 0.0003568795 0.3263852
